query: Consider the following context: Temper embrittlement, characterized by a dramatic loss of ductility within a narrow temperature window, is ubiquitous in conventional alloys but is not reported in compositionally complex or high‐entropy alloy systems. In that context, which material can be used for ductile–brittle–ductile transition, and why?

generation.hypothesis: A compositionally complex alloy system, specifically a high-entropy alloy, can be used for a ductile–brittle–ductile transition due to its resistance to temper embrittlement.
generation.material_initial_state: High-entropy alloy in its annealed state
generation.intervention: Temperature-controlled mechanical testing with molecular dynamics simulations
generation.conditions: Testing within the narrow temperature window where temper embrittlement occurs in conventional alloys
generation.structural_mediator: Grain boundary structure and segregation of elements
generation.mechanism: The high-entropy alloy's resistance to temper embrittlement is attributed to its unique grain boundary structure and segregation of elements, which hinders the formation of brittle phases
generation.predicted_outcome: A 30% increase in ductility compared to conventional alloys within the narrow temperature window
generation.baseline: Conventional alloys' ductility at the same temperature range
generation.uncertainty: The exact mechanism of temper embrittlement resistance in high-entropy alloys is not fully understood and may depend on specific alloy compositions and processing conditions

falsification_experiment.design: Temperature-controlled mechanical testing with molecular dynamics simulations on high-entropy alloys and conventional alloys
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the high-entropy alloy exhibits a ductility decrease of more than 20% within the narrow temperature window, the hypothesis is falsified

frame.system: conventional alloys vs. compositionally complex or high‐entropy alloy systems, in their initial or annealed state
frame.goal: understanding the ductile–brittle–ductile transition and identifying a suitable material for it
frame.limitation: temper embrittlement causing a dramatic loss of ductility within a narrow temperature window in conventional alloys
frame.regime: various temperatures, specifically the narrow temperature window where temper embrittlement occurs
prior_attempts: use of conventional alloys, which fell short due to temper embrittlement

families.principle: Real-time or high-resolution observation of material behavior to reveal underlying mechanisms
families.best_lever: in-situ transmission electron microscopy (TEM) or scanning electron microscopy (SEM)

families.principle: Integration of experimental and simulation approaches to validate and refine understanding of material behavior
families.best_lever: coupling temperature-controlled mechanical testing with molecular dynamics simulations

families.principle: Systematic manipulation of variables to isolate cause-and-effect relationships
Computational modeling of material behavior at the atomic or mesoscopic scale to predict properties and behavior
cues_for: compositionally complex or high‐entropy alloy systems
families.best_lever: molecular dynamics simulations of alloy systems
